findings.issue: Rebuilt dist/ while the old server process still held the port, then spent ~6 turns diagnosing an unstyled screenshot that was a stale process serving deleted hashed assets.
findings.suggestion: Check running processes / kill servers before rebuilding and restarting, or verify the served HTML's asset hashes against the new build first.

findings.issue: A thinking block spent itself re-reading and second-guessing its own earlier tool output (Vite version 8.3.5 vs 8.3.3) instead of just re-running npm view.
findings.suggestion: Re-run the cheap, deterministic command immediately instead of arguing with a memory of its output.

findings.issue: Guessed GitHub repository names/organizations, causing two failed clone prompts before finding gracile-web/starter-projects.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the canonical repo URL from the npm package metadata or a web search before cloning.

findings.issue: Two throwaway calls: a malformed sed pipeline that produced no output, and an assumption that Python PIL was installed.
findings.suggestion: Quick capability checks (pip list / verify the command prints something) before scripting against optional dependencies.

summary: An exemplary process: the agent digested the spec, tests, fixtures and reference designs up front, verified the framework's build behavior from its source to honor the no-build-time-fetching constraint, and passed the entire 54-test suite on its first run with zero fix cycles. Verification went beyond the suite — screenshots at both required widths compared against references, with a follow-up full test run after the last CSS edit. The only blemishes are a handful of self-inflicted tool-call and process-management detours that cost a few turns but no correctness.
